increment_paragraph: **OPENSSL-FREE-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS (2026-11-20).** The named follow-up recorded by OPENSSL-FREE-SESSION-REMOVE-INVOCATION. quirin-provider-openssl declares the nine X509_LOOKUP_meth_set_* setters from X509_LOOKUP_meth_new (3.5) with the NAME check, fetch_docs.py snapshots (1.1.1, 3.0, 3.5; none at 1.0.2) and pinned prototypes (x509_lookup_slots.qv, keys x509_lookup_method_st.lookup_meth_*, spelled after the setter so no key segment is a common pre-pass token; range documented 1.1.1 because HISTORY's 1.1.0i is a letter release the version vocabulary cannot spell). X509_STORE_free, SSL_CTX_free and SSL_free state the lookup method's shutdown and free slots beside their drop (actual _) and name the new library-value premise openssl_builtin_lookup_methods. A store's twelve X509_STORE_set_* slots are not run at its free (its cleanup function runs at X509_STORE_CTX_cleanup) and are not stated there. A source survey of OpenSSL 3.5.5 found further callbacks the frees run on objects they free in turn (keys' provider, method and engine functions, the client certificate engine, a CRL's method, the async wait context's cleanup functions, the QUIC TLS callbacks, a QUIC object's free, not traced), so by the fail-closed rule the frees keep openssl_unstated_callback_slots, in a statement of their own naming exactly that remainder (it drops the handshake kinds and ex_data, which openssl_ex_data_callbacks covers); X509_STORE_free, which read it silently, gains the premise. contracts.lock: 9 entries added and 3 digests changed (X509_STORE_free, SSL_CTX_free, SSL_free); pinned and library_versions unchanged. No gateway code changed. Lean: new QCore.OpensslFreeIndirectCallbacks, audited. ledger.title: Callbacks the OpenSSL frees run on objects they free in turn whose setters no declaration states
ledger.text: Found by OPENSSL-FREE-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS (source survey of OpenSSL 3.5.5). X509_STORE_free, SSL_CTX_free and SSL_free keep openssl_unstated_callback_slots, whose statement on the frees (UNSTATED_FREE_STATEMENT) names: a key's provider key management free function (a dispatch table, no setter); a legacy key's EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD free (EVP_PKEY_asn1_set_free); the finish function of a key's RSA_METHOD, DSA_METHOD, DH_METHOD or EC_KEY_METHOD (RSA_meth_set_finish and siblings); the finish and destroy functions of a key's ENGINE and of the context's client certificate engine (ENGINE_set_finish_function, ENGINE_set_destroy_function; SSL_CTX_set_client_cert_engine has no 3.5 page); a CRL's X509_CRL_METHOD crl_free (X509_CRL_METHOD_new, no 3.5 page); the async wait context's fd cleanup functions (ASYNC_WAIT_CTX_set_wait_fd); the QUIC TLS crypto_release_rcd callback (SSL_set_quic_tls_cbs, a dispatch table, run by RECORD_LAYER_clear); and whatever a QUIC object's free runs, which was not traced past quic_impl.c. DISCHARGE: declare the documented setters as slot registrations (RSA/DSA/DH meth_set_finish, EC_KEY_METHOD_set_init, ENGINE_set_finish_function/destroy_function, EVP_PKEY_asn1_set_free, ASYNC_WAIT_CTX_set_wait_fd) and state their slots at the frees with library-value premises; for dispatch tables (providers, QUIC TLS) and undocumented setters a user decision on a premise or on admitting the pinned source; trace the QUIC free path. Only when every item is stated may the frees drop the premise. Size: large; partly needs a user decision.

ledger.title: X509_free, EVP_PKEY_free, PKCS12_free and ENGINE_free read their method and engine callbacks silently
ledger.text: Found by OPENSSL-FREE-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS. These declarations name only openssl_ex_data_callbacks, yet the last free of a key runs its provider key management free function, its EVP_PKEY_ASN1_METHOD free and its RSA/DSA/DH/EC_KEY method finish function and ENGINE finish (EVP_PKEY_free, p_lib.c and rsa_lib.c 3.5.5); X509_free and PKCS12_free free certificates and so their public keys; ENGINE_free runs the engine's destroy function (ENGINE_set_destroy_function). No premise names these callbacks. Metadata only (premises move no verdict), but a declaration resting on an unstated assumption is a provenance gap. DISCHARGE: name openssl_unstated_callback_slots in the statement of a free (UNSTATED_FREE_STATEMENT) on each, with the checker's expectation and the reviewed lock diff, or state the slots as OPENSSL-FREE-REMAINING-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS does. Size: small.

OPENSSL-FREE-INDIRECT-CALLBACKS declared the nine X509_LOOKUP_meth_set_* setters (x509_lookup_slots.qv, keys x509_lookup_method_st.lookup_meth_*) and the library-value premise openssl_builtin_lookup_methods, and stated only the shutdown and free slots, at the frees. The handshake's lookups (X509_STORE_CTX_get_by_subject reaches get_by_subject; 3.5.5 has no setter for get_by_subject_ex or ctrl_ex, so a user method runs get_by_subject) remain this card. The built-in premise's statement names a lookup of a store the call frees; the handshake needs it widened to a lookup the call reads through. SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations and SSL_CTX_set_default_verify_paths reach only built-in lookups (X509_STORE_add_lookup reuses a lookup by method identity) and read that silently too.
